description: Reusable intent questions. A finding names one with intent_id; one recorded answer then resolves every record that asks it. Answers are stored on the reviewer's machine with omgs intent answer, never in the reviewed repository.

questions.question: Is this resource meant to be readable without signing in?
questions.why: An unauthenticated read is a finding only when the resource is private; public catalogs and status pages are intended.

questions.question: May a member of one workspace or tenant ever read another workspace's records through this route?
questions.why: Shared or federated workspaces exist; without that intent, any cross-tenant read is an isolation break.

questions.question: Which roles are allowed to perform this action?
questions.why: A missing role check matters only when the action is meant to be restricted.

questions.question: Is hiding this screen in the browser meant to be the only control, or must the server refuse the request too?
questions.why: A UI-only gate is acceptable for cosmetics and never for protected data or actions.

questions.question: Which senders may call this webhook, and must every delivery be signed and fresh?
questions.why: Unsigned or replayable webhooks are findings when only one provider is meant to trigger the handler.

questions.question: May an external feed lower a security minimum (for example an OS version floor) automatically, or only raise it?
questions.why: A feed that can move a minimum backwards weakens policy without review; many teams intend raise-only.

questions.question: When an imported rule uses a filter the tool does not support, should the rule be dropped (fail closed) or applied without the filter?
questions.why: Applying a rule without its filter widens its scope, for example a group-limited mapping becoming universal.

questions.question: Who is allowed to supply the manifest, project, or configuration file whose values reach a generated script?
questions.why: Values becoming code is a finding when the file can come from someone less trusted than the person running the tool.
answers: only the operator running the tool

questions.question: Must a dry run be free of side effects, including executing commands built from input?
questions.why: A dry run that still executes manifest-controlled commands breaks the safety the flag promises.

questions.question: Which URL schemes may reach managed browser policy through this export?
questions.why: Schemes such as javascript: or file: in managed bookmarks or start pages are rarely intended.

questions.question: Are imported files trusted to be well formed, or must the importer bound nesting and size?
questions.why: Unbounded recursion is a denial of service only when imports can come from untrusted sources.

questions.question: Which directories may this tool delete from, and may the user control any parent of those paths?
questions.why: Deletion through a user-controlled parent or symlink is a finding when the tool runs with more privilege than the user.
answers: any path the invoking user owns

questions.question: Must every installed payload be signed by one expected team and match the requested version?
questions.why: A helper that installs as root with a skipped signer or version check runs attacker code with root.
answers: expected team and version always required

questions.question: May an older version ever replace a newer installed version?
questions.why: Downgrades reintroduce fixed vulnerabilities; most updaters intend never, or only with an explicit rollback flag.
answers: only with an explicit rollback action

questions.question: Must the requested resource belong to the authenticated identity or an explicitly authorized delegate?
questions.why: A valid identity must still be bound to the selected resource and operation.

questions.question: Must an unavailable or unsupported security decision stop the protected operation?
questions.why: Error handling can widen authority when unknown is treated as permission.

questions.question: Which callers may connect to each IPC listener and invoke each exported operation?
questions.why: Connection admission and operation authorization can have different allowed populations.

questions.question: Which callers may receive each stored secret, and may credentials leave the privileged service?
questions.why: Permission to request an operation does not imply permission to read its credentials.

questions.question: Which privileged operations may each caller perform and on which resources?
questions.why: An admitted connection still needs per-operation and resource authorization.
